thread:
Jordan H: Quick ask — can we get a one-off exception to the holiday blackout for Dec 24-26? One engineer on my team ended up double-booked on parental travel and the oncall swap fell through.

Devin (Eng Manager): Oof. Who's impacted and what coverage plan did you try?

Jordan H: It's Anika. She already used most of her carryover earlier this year. We set up a buddy backup but the buddy is traveling too. I can cover part of the night shifts but not the whole stack.

Amy (Oncall Lead): @Devin @Jordan H what shift chunks are we talking about? We can do partial swaps but need clear handover.

Jordan H: Nightly windows 2200-0400 PST on 24/25 and 25/26. I can take 2200-0200 both nights, need someone for 0200-0400.

Devin (Eng Manager): I can probably rearrange my schedule to cover one of those 0200-0400 slots but not both. Any volunteers from the SRE rotation?

PeopleOps Bot: Reminder: company holiday blackout dates are in effect Dec 20-27. Time-off requests in that window require manager approval + People Ops sign-off per policy 3.2.

Maria (People Ops): Thanks for the heads-up. We do allow emergency exceptions for coverage-critical roles if manager attests to mitigation plan. Please file a formal request in the TimeOff app and include: 1) shift coverage matrix, 2) why Anika cannot move dates, 3) whether accrual/carryover is being used.

Jordan H: Filed request: Request ID 20261234. Pasted coverage plan in the form. Quick copy of the snippet I added:

```
Coverage plan:
- Dec 24 22:00-02:00 PST: Jordan H
- Dec 24 02:00-04:00 PST: Devin (cover slot)
- Dec 25 22:00-02:00 PST: Jordan H
- Dec 25 02:00-04:00 PST: Volunteer needed (open)
Fallback: Push non-critical batch jobs to standby, page escalation policy set to on-call escalation 2.
```

Amy (Oncall Lead): I'll ping the SRE rotation in #eng-oncall right now and ask for volunteers for the open slot.

Devin (Eng Manager): If no volunteer, I can swap a non-prod duty with Lee and pick up the last 0200-0400 on the 25th. Prefer that to making Anika cancel travel.

Maria (People Ops): Good. When you submit the TimeOff request, choose "Exceptional Approval" and attach manager approval note. I can fast-track sign-off once I see the coverage plan and that at least one slot has a named backup.

Frank (Payroll): Quick note on accruals — if Anika's accrual is short and you approve unpaid PTO, mark the days as "Unpaid Exception" in the system. That avoids carryover accounting errors at year-end.

Jordan H: Thanks, Frank. Her accruals show 4 hours short for those dates; I indicated "use carryover + unpaid for remainder" in the request per policy.

Maria (People Ops): That's fine. Two process reminders: 1) exceptions are granted conservatively — we prefer swaps over exceptions; 2) approvals before the day-of are required. We'll aim to respond within 48 hours.

Amy (Oncall Lead): Volunteer found: Lee will take 25th 02:00-04:00. Tagging @Lee.

Jordan H: Awesome — updated Request ID 20261234 with Lee's name. Anything else needed?

Maria (People Ops): All set from People Ops side. I'll add the approval note and mark it as "Blackout Exception Approved: coverage verified". Please ensure the rotation calendar is updated and add handover in the incident channel.

Jordan H: Will do. Thanks everyone :raised_hands:

Devin (Eng Manager): Appreciate the quick help. Glad we could avoid Anika canceling travel.

PeopleOps Bot: Request 20261234 status changed to APPROVED by Maria (People Ops).

Jordan H: Copy that — closing the loop.

Maria (People Ops): Filing: policy reference PTO-3.2, exception note ID EX-2026-11. Keeping this on file for audit.

Frank (Payroll): I'll note the unpaid portion in payroll feed so year-end reports are accurate.

Jordan H: Thanks all.
